prerequisites: Programming knowledge in MATLAB, Python or similar language

learning_outcomes.text: Possess the capacity to design, develop, implement, manage and improve products, systems and processes in the different industrial fields, using appropriate analytical, computational or experimental techniques.
Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them while working in multidisciplinary teams.
Understand the impact of engineering on the environment, the sustainable development of society and the importance of working in a professional and responsible environment.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess the learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Incorporate ICT and Industrial Engineering technologies and tools into their professional activities.
Know and apply basic science and technology knowledge to the practice of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge and capacities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.
Basic knowledge of the finite element method and mechanical vibrations in engineering.
Use Matlab as a calculation tool.

syllabus_topics: Critical speed of a rotating shaft
Application of vibration measurement to machine maintenance
Topic 6 - Introduction to the Finite Element Method
Introduction. Coordinates and shape functions. Potential energy approach. Element assembly. Properties of stiffness matrices. Temperature change effects. Articulated Systems. Beams and Frames
Topic 10 - Introduction to simulation using ANSYS
assessment_rules: The final grade is the maximum between the progressive evaluation system (C_PROG) and the global final test system (C_GLOBAL). The course is passed if the final grade is 5.0 or higher. In the extraordinary call, a single written exam determines the final grade, requiring a minimum of 5 points out of 10. Progressive Evaluation (C_PROG) consists of two partial tests (PROG1, PROG2, each 2 points) and a final exercises test (EJER, 6 points, with a minimum of 2.4 points). A voluntary laboratory practice (VOL) can add up to 1 additional point. Global Evaluation (C_GLOBAL) consists of an exercises exam (EJER, 6 points, minimum 2.4 points) and a theoretical exam (TEOR, 4 points, no minimum).
